review: 1:2 לְכָל־טוֹב וָחֶסֶד רַב — 'for all good and abundant grace'; the Arabic لِلْخَيْرِ وَاللُّطْفِ الْعَظِيم is a pair of nouns, and Hebrew keeps the pair while רַב fills the line.
2:2–2:3 נָתַתָּ לָנוּ חַיִּים / מֵת בַּעֲדֵנוּ פִּדְיוֹן — the Arabic إِذْ مَاتَ عَنَّا فِدْيَةً is one clause; Hebrew splits it so that 'ransom' lands on the cadence.
3:2 לִפְנֵי זְמָן עוֹלָמִים — 'before the time of ages', for قَبْلَ الزَّمَانِ الْأَزَلِيّ; the construct is the biblical way of saying 'before everlasting time' (Ps 55:20, מִקֶּדֶם).
4:2 הִשְׁלַמְתָּנוּ — 'You made us whole/reconciled'; the Arabic صَالَحْتَنَا is 'reconciled', and the hiph'il of שלם carries both 'complete' and 'at peace'.
5:2 כִּרְצוֹן חַסְדְּךָ הַטּוֹב — 'according to the good will of Your grace', for بِحَسْبِ قَصْدِ نِعْمَتِك; רָצוֹן is the glossary word for God's purpose.
